findings.title: hosts.map users lack destinationCalendar, so teamDestinationCalendars stays empty
findings.body: In the new loadUsers(), when the event has hosts, `users` is built via `hosts.map(({ user, isFixed }) => ({ ...user, isFixed }))`. The `user` record on each host is whatever Prisma returned for the relation; no explicit `select`/`include` is added, so relation fields like `destinationCalendar` are not present on those `user` objects. Downstream, `teamMemberPromises` does `if (isTeamEventType && eventType.schedulingType === "COLLECTIVE" && user.destinationCalendar)` and pushes to `teamDestinationCalendars` — this will always be undefined for host-loaded users, so `teamDestinationCalendars` ends up empty for COLLECTIVE team events. The whole point of this PR (multiple hosts receiving calendar events) silently fails whenever hosts come from the `eventType.hosts` relation.

findings.title: evt.destinationCalendar?.push silently no-ops when null
findings.body: Right above, `destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` is set. The follow-up `if (isTeamEventType && eventType.schedulingType === "COLLECTIVE") { evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars); }` uses optional chaining on a potentially null array — `null?.push` is just `undefined`, it does nothing and does not warn. For any COLLECTIVE event without an event-type or organizer destination calendar, no team members' destination calendars are attached to `evt`, even though they were collected into `teamDestinationCalendars`. Replace `?.push(...)` with an explicit `evt.destinationCalendar ??= []; evt.destinationCalendar.push(...)` (or build the final array once and assign it).

findings.title: Only first destination calendar is persisted on the booking
findings.body: The booking `data` block writes `destinationCalendar: evt.destinationCalendar && evt.destinationCalendar.length > 0 ? { connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id } } : undefined`. The Booking schema has a single `destinationCalendar` relation, so only the first entry in `evt.destinationCalendar` is persisted. The PR’s stated goal is to invite every host to their own calendar, but on any later operation (reschedule, cancel, edit-location, request-reschedule) the booking record exposes only one destination. The other per-host calendar references survive only as BookingReference rows; deleting the booking.destinationCalendar connect for the event-type even on first creation breaks the previously persisted id reference for non-collective callers and silently drops the per-host mapping for re-runs. Either the schema needs to become a join table, or the booking should record which host’s calendar it was set under and consumers must be updated accordingly — this PR ships neither.

findings.title: updateEvent fallback finds by externalId === externalCalendarId (its own falsy arg)
findings.body: In `updateEvent`: `const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. The branch only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, but then `.find` compares each calendar’s `externalId` against that same falsy value — it can essentially never match, so `selectedCalendar` will always be `undefined` in the fallback path and the update will fall back to whatever `calendarId` ends up being (`undefined` here, since the destructuring doesn’t define one). This is a regression vs. the old line `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`, which at least returned the first calendar’s externalId. The intended fallback was almost certainly `event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId` (or matching by `credentialId`). Effect: any Google calendar update that reaches this code without a non-empty `externalCalendarId` will misroute or attempt to operate against `calendarId: undefined`.

findings.title: deleteEvent fallback also searches by externalId === externalCalendarId
findings.body: Same defect as in `updateEvent`. `const calendarId = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;` — when `externalCalendarId` is null/empty the `find` predicate compares each calendar’s externalId against that same null/empty value, so the find never matches and the fallback always yields `undefined`. The eventual ternary `calendarId ? calendarId : defaultCalendarId` then drops to `"primary"`, which is the wrong calendar for multi-host events and can delete from the wrong account or simply 404. Either use `event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId` for the fallback or restrict the lookup to a credentialId-keyed match.

findings.title: Calendar.createEvent signature requires credentialId; other implementations still take one arg
findings.body: The `Calendar` interface now declares `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent, credentialId: number): Promise<NewCalendarEventType>`, but the other concrete implementations were not updated: `BaseCalendarService.createEvent(event: CalendarEvent)` in packages/lib/CalendarService.ts (line 125), `LarkCalendarService.createEvent(event: CalendarEvent)` in packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts (line 125), and `Office365CalendarService.createEvent(event: CalendarEvent)` in packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts (line 72) all declare `implements Calendar` and define `createEvent` with a single parameter. This is an interface/implementation mismatch that TypeScript will reject on build; every consumer of these apps (e.g., `createAllCalendarEvents` in EventManager) currently calls `calendar.createEvent(calEvent)` without the new `credentialId`, so those code paths will not compile against the interface. Either make `credentialId` optional in the interface and update only Google, or update the three other services and all call sites to pass the credential id.

findings.title: Organization slug/requestSlug logic is inverted and out of scope
findings.body: This PR is supposed to change only the destinationCalendar handling, but this file was modified and the change inverts behavior: previously `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` set the org slug when billing was disabled, and `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { requestedSlug: slug })` set the metadata requestedSlug when billing was enabled. The new code is `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` (slug now set when billing is enabled — opposite of before) plus `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { requestedSlug: slug } : {})` (requestedSlug now conditional, where it used to also be set unconditionally on the top-level create). Organizations created while billing is disabled will now have no slug at all instead of the previous behavior, which breaks subdomain routing for non-billing orgs. This deserves to be a separate PR with proper justification and migration handling, not a drive-by change hidden inside a calendar refactor.

findings.title: loadUsers aggressively throws on empty dynamicUserList and is no longer required to return users
findings.body: The new `loadUsers` wraps everything in try/catch and throws HttpError(500, "Unable to load users") for any non-HttpError/non-Prisma error, and adds new preconditions that the previous version lacked: `if (!Array.isArray(dynamicUserList) || dynamicUserList.length === 0) throw new Error("dynamicUserList is not properly defined or empty.")` and `if (!Array.isArray(hosts)) throw new Error("eventType.hosts is not properly defined.")`. Empty `dynamicUserList` was previously allowed to fall through to a normal empty result; a route that legitimately resolves no users (e.g., data issues) will now return 500/400 instead of being handled by upstream `ensureAvailableUsers` guards. Also, `return users.length ? users : eventType.users` evaluates eventType.users only after spreading hosts — for a non-host regular event this works, but for a team event with `eventType.schedulingType=ROUND_ROBIN` and no hosts it now returns the legacy `eventType.users` array and silently bypasses the host semantics the rest of the code expects.

findings.title: Team member shape adds unknown firstName/lastName empty fields
findings.body: `teamMemberPromises` returns `firstName: "", lastName: ""` for every team member, but the `Person` type in `@calcom/types/Calendar` has no such keys (only `name`, `email`, `timeZone`, `language`, `username`, `id`, `bookingId`, `locale`, `timeFormat`, `bookingSeat`). Any strict object-literal usage would fail, and email/SMS renderers that iterate the object will get the empty strings. This was added without updating the type definition or any consumer — either the fields need to be added to `Person` and used by templates, or the spread of dead keys should be removed.
